examples: I have never built an *algorithm* before. (present perfect + never for experience)
She has just learned the new *interface*. (present perfect + just for a recent action)
The bank has already updated its *encryption*. (present perfect + already)
Have you ever tested your *bandwidth* at home? (present perfect + ever for experience)
They have just launched a *virtual* museum tour. (present perfect + just)
I bought this *sensor* yesterday. (past simple + a finished time)
Have you made a *backup* yet? (present perfect + yet)
They *upgraded* their system last month. (past simple + a finished time)
I have never changed my *privacy* settings. (present perfect + never)
The *robot* arrived last Monday. (past simple + a finished time)
grammar.explanation:
The **present perfect** is formed with **have/has + past participle**. Use it for past experiences when you do not say exactly when they happened. I have tested a cleaning robot at home, and I have never used an interface this simple before.

Use the **present perfect** for recent actions that have a result now. It goes with **yet**, **already**, and **just**. She has just made a backup of her files. Have you upgraded your phone yet?

Use the **past simple** for finished actions when you say or know when they happened. I installed a sensor in my hallway last week. The company released the big upgrade in June.

Never use the **present perfect** with a past time expression like **yesterday** or **last year**. Say I checked my privacy settings yesterday, not I have checked my privacy settings yesterday.
